1 id section_1 title "Prerequisite: DNA Directionality and Base Pairing" content "≈45 sec. Review antiparallel double helix, 5'→3' polarity, complementary A–T/G–C, and semiconservative copying. Animation: two DNA strands as colored tracks with 5'/3' arrowheads; parental duplex unzips into two templates." example: "A zipper with two colored sides: each side becomes a template for a new matching side; the 5'/3' arrows on the two strands point opposite ways."
2 "Initiation at Multiple Origins" content "≈50 sec. Eukaryotes use multiple origins of replication. Origin recognition proteins open DNA; helicase unwinds to form replication forks/bubbles. Animation: chromosome with many glowing origins, bubbles expanding bidirectionally." example "A long train route with many stations starting repair simultaneously, so the whole chromosome is copied faster than from one station."
3 "Unwinding and Priming: The Starting Machinery" content "≈55 sec. Animation: fork moving, with enzyme icons and primer as small flag." example "Helicase is a snowplow; SSB proteins are safety clips; topoisomerase is a swivel; primase places a starter block so the builder polymerase can begin."
4 "Elongation: Leading and Lagging Strands" content "≈75 sec. DNA polymerase adds nucleotides 5'→3' using template 3'→5'. Leading strand synthesizes continuously toward fork; lagging strand synthesizes discontinuously away from fork as Okazaki fragments, each with RNA primer. Animation: one smooth arrow and several short arrows, with polarity arrows labeled." example "Leading strand = continuous highway lane; lagging strand = stop-and-go lane made of short Okazaki fragment cars, all built in the same 5'→3' direction but on opposite template orientations."
5 "Maturation, Proofreading, and Chromatin Assembly" content "≈60 sec. RNase H/FEN1 remove RNA primers; DNA polymerase fills gaps; DNA ligase seals nicks. Polymerase proofreads by 3'→5' exonuclease. New DNA is packaged with histones into nucleosomes. Animation: primer removal, gap filling, ligase zipper; nucleosomes spooling." example "Editing a document: remove placeholder text (RNA primer), type correct text (DNA fill), and staple pages (ligase); proofreading is spell-check; histones are spools for storage."
6 "Telomeres and Summary" content "≈55 sec. Linear eukaryotic ends cannot be fully replicated by standard polymerase, so telomerase extends telomeres in some cells. Summarize: multiple origins, bidirectional forks, semiconservative, leading/lagging, enzymes, proofreading, chromatin. Animation: end-replication problem at chromosome tip, telomerase adding repeats, then summary wheel." example "A shoelace: telomeres are protective plastic tips; telomerase is a tip-repair machine in stem/germ cells, while most somatic cells have limited tip repair."
